deepdive.sec: Captive-power IPP & merchant thermal generation (with Ferro-alloys + African resource/agri diversification)

bull_bear.body:
- $50m Nava Global buyback completed via Maamba dividend upstreaming.
- Stated priority: retain cash for greenfield/expansion funding first, then corporate actions (generous dividends/buybacks "to boost shareholder confidence").
- Net debt ~$200m at 9M FY26 — modest given asset base.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Domestic merchant power price/demand decline (~12% YoY exchange price drop).
- Ferro-alloys at near-breakeven; cyclical, low-margin.
- Maamba arrears ($30.5m outstanding) and Zambia sovereign/FX exposure (other income swings on FX).
- Long-gestation diversification (avocado 8 yrs, sugar to 2028, lithium/Ivory Coast unproven) ties up capital with distant payback.
- Solar payback 10–12 years — low IRR optionality.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, candid; openly acknowledged domestic power weakness and ferro-alloy underperformance rather than spinning. Clear capital-allocation discipline (buyback funded by subsidiary dividend, debt kept modest). Founder family (Devineni) deeply involved across operations and strategy.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated profitability is highly leveraged to a single asset (Maamba PLF) — 97% PLF this quarter flatters margins; normalization or shutdowns will compress.
- A large chunk of the other-income beat (~INR30 cr) is non-cash FX and not sustainable — headline PAT growth overstates operating momentum.
- The India business is effectively being de-risked into long-term PPAs (TN at INR5.2/kWh) to escape volatile exchange pricing.
- Significant hidden optionality (65-acre Nacharam land, lithium, Ivory Coast minerals) carried at no/low recognized value.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Nava Global (subsidiary) declared a dividend of US$15 Mn during the quarter.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Maamba Energy (MEL)**: core profit engine; 97% PLF; arrears down, $30.5m outstanding receivable remaining; 300MW Phase-2 expansion underway.
- **Nava Global**: completed $50m buyback funded by Maamba dividends; remains 100% Nava-owned (buyback reduced capital, no ownership change).
- **Indian power**: planned shutdowns at several plants this quarter dampened PLF; domestic price/demand softening.
- **Ferro-alloys**: weak profitability; manganese sourced mostly outside India, minimal MOIL exposure (only small fines, no lumps) so MOIL's 5% price hike is immaterial.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary stock(s) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domestic merchant power price down ~12% YoY | NAVA · 513023 (via LT PPAs like TN 60MW) | NAVA · 513023 (domestic merchant exposure) | Mitigation via long-term contracts cushions but caps upside; net mild negative — Med |
| Zambia 400MW+ thermal/solar build-out | NAVA · 513023 | — | $490m capex with FY27-28 revenue ($195–216m run-rate) materially grows earnings base — High |
| Ferro-alloy weakness despite +8% price | — | NAVA · 513023 | Segment near breakeven; structurally low-margin drag — Med |
| MOIL manganese ore price +5% (Feb) | — | Silico-manganese producers reliant on MOIL (code unverified) | NAVA largely insulated (sources outside India), so neutral-to-positive for NAVA vs peers — Med |
| African resource optionality (lithium, Ivory Coast minerals) | NAVA · 513023 | — | Free optionality if discoveries materialize; unproven — Low |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Diversified group operating across Ferro Alloys, Energy (India and Zambia via MEL), Mining, and emerging agri-businesses (avocado plantation, integrated sugar project) under the tagline 'Diverse Businesses. Unified Vision.'
- Manufacturing/energy operations are certified to ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 and ISO 50001.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [Zambia Arbitration Receivables] MEL Zambia's receivables under an arbitration award stood at US$18.4 Mn as of 30-Jun-26, reducing to US$13.4 Mn as of the presentation date on US$15.0 Mn of realization; the associated ECL provision reversal is now minimal as ZESCO arrears near full realization.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA margin expansion to 48.3% almost entirely MEL PLF-driven (97%), not cost reversal.
- Domestic exchange power price down ~12% YoY — margin headwind mitigated via long-term contracts.
- Ferro-alloys structurally low-margin; +8% price recovery into Q4 but EBIT near breakeven.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- PAT +83.5% QoQ; EBITDA margin 34.5% → 48.3% QoQ (MEL 97% PLF).
- Mining revenue +16.6% QoQ on higher volumes.
- Other income INR26 cr → INR70.4 cr QoQ (mostly FX, sustainable ~INR40 cr).
- Ferro-alloy EBIT ~INR2 cr → ~breakeven QoQ; pricing +8% into Q4.
- 300MW thermal spend ~$190m cumulative ($90–100m in 9M); solar ~$10m.
- Maamba arrears reduced; $30.5m outstanding remaining.
- $50m Nava Global buyback completed (new this quarter).
- New TN 5-yr PPA (60MW Odisha, INR5.2/kWh) referenced (disclosed prior quarter, progressing).
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **Q4 FY26 Indian power**: "more or less fully committed" on tie-ups for summer.
- **Q1 FY27 Indian power**: in process of tying up most surplus quantities.
- **Ferro-alloys**: pricing +8% from Q3 into current Q4; mgmt expects prices "stable" rather than rising sharply — low-margin but good top line.
- **300MW thermal (Zambia) + 100MW solar**: full-year operations from FY27-28. Full-year revenue at steady state — thermal $180–200m, solar $15–16m.
- **Sugar (KSL) processing unit**: complete ~April 2028 (mid-2028).
- **Avocado**: full production from all 4 divisions over an 8-year horizon; significant revenue contribution 4–5 years out.
outlook.title: Guidance (forward)

outlook.body:
- Long-term 5-year bilateral PPA with Tamil Nadu for 60MW IPP plant in Odisha at INR5.2/kWh.
- Targeting similar long-term/short-term allocations for other domestic units to reduce exchange-price volatility.
- Maamba supplying Phase 1 & Phase 2 PPAs in Zambia; govt diversifying away from hydro.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- 100MW Zambia solar ($90m capex, 10–12 yr payback); potential additional solar phase later.
- Avocado plantation (4 divisions × 275 ha; first pilot crop 140 MT; $55m commitment).
- Kawambwa Sugar Ltd ($100m commitment).
- Ivory Coast 360 sq km mineral concession — under exploration, no discovery disclosed.
- Lithium mines in Africa — exploration stage.
- Nacharam land (65 acres, Hyderabad) — rising market value, unmonetized optionality.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Cash-rich, founder-run conglomerate where Zambian thermal IPP (Maamba) drives consolidated profit and funds a multi-pronged diversification (300MW thermal expansion, 100MW solar, sugar, avocado, lithium/mineral exploration), while the domestic Indian power and ferro-alloy businesses face a softening price cycle.

open.item: Q2 employee cost jumped to INR111.6 crores (from INR65.77 cr) on salary revisions (effective 1 April) and RSU fair valuation one-offs; not expected to rise beyond this level
At full-year operations, 300 MW thermal expected revenue US$180-200 million and 100 MW solar US$15-16 million
Per presentation, solar plant completion targeted H1 of next financial year and thermal (300 MW) H2, with full-year operations of both from FY2027-28
MEL 100% tax exemption continues to end of FY26, after which it moves to 50% exemption for the next three years (from FY27)

Silico Manganese production is expected to be lower in FY 2026-27 with the announced shutdown of furnaces at Odisha operations for April - June 2026, against installed flexibility to produce up to approximately 160,000 MT.
The balance of the ZESCO receivable under the Arbitral Award, reduced to US$ 28.0 million by March 2026, is expected to be realised by the middle of calendar 2026.
The 100 MW Maamba Solar project is scheduled to commence commissioning in Q2 FY27.
Total capex of the 100 MW solar project is US$ 90 million, of which US$ 63 million of debt funding has been tied up.
Commission the 100 MW solar project under Maamba Solar Energy Limited, with total capex of US$ 90 million and US$ 63 million of debt tied up.
Commission the avocado packhouse to strengthen the ability to manage quality, storage and market timing.
Avocado plantation is expected to yield approximately 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27, with volumes expected to approximately double each year thereafter through 2034.
The 300 MW Phase II expansion at Maamba is targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27.

Avocado fruit yield from Division A is expected to scale to 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27 from approximately over 150 MT in FY 2025-26, with progressive scaling thereafter and Division B expected to give a trial yield in the current year.
Reduced daytime merchant tariffs on power exchanges from higher solar generation, together with a projected below-average monsoon and dry spells, have to be watched for remunerative tariffs.
Lower ECL reversal and appreciation of the Zambian Kwacha will impact the profitability of MEL's power division in the current year.
Management does not anticipate any reason for ferro alloy prices to fall meaningfully below the preceding year on a full-year basis.
Captive power tariffs have been revised downwards on lower Singareni coal prices and better Odisha plant parameters, with the positive effect to be seen in FY 2026-27.

Commission MEL's Phase II 300 MW brownfield thermal power plant in Zambia, with a capex outlay of USD 400 million of which US$ 290 million of debt is tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions.
Phase II 300 MW plant carries a capex outlay of USD 400 million with US$ 290 million of debt funding already tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions.
The Phase II 300 MW thermal expansion and the avocado plantation projects crossed the 50% overall progress mark during the year and are to near completion phase by March 2027.
